newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn futures end lower on weather forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn futures end lower on weather forecasts.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended lower on Thursday, hit by perceptions weather patterns were ideal for corn planting and development, traders said.
"The weather is behind all of this," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "The weather is bearish with a capital "B". Cool summers, early plantings equal record yields."

Lespinasse and others continued to draw comparisons between this year's crop prospects and 1994's record production. They noted both crops were planted early and temperatures during much of the 1994 growing season were normal to below normal.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook released late Wednesday predicted normal to below normal temperatures with above normal precipitation for most of the western Corn Belt.

Corn had opened higher, in line with gains in soybeans, on USDA's weekly export sales figures which came in above trade expectations. USDA on Thursday said for the week ended May 15, U.S. net export sales of corn totaled 614,600 tonnes, well above trade expectations for 350,000 to 450,000 tonnes.
Corn ended 3-1/2 to one cent per bushel lower with July off 3-1/2 at $2.73-1/4 a bushel.
On the day, Farmers Commodities Corp sold five million bushels July, Cargill Inc sold one million July and bought 2.5 million, traders said.
Tenco Inc spread at least 3.5 million bushels December/July at 14 to 14-1/2 cents, premium July.
In options trade, LIT bought 600 September $2.40 puts at 11-3/4 to 12 cents and CIS bought 400 December $2.70 calls at 13-3/4 to 14 cents.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 54,579.
